text: Because we do not expect any acknowledgement. Indeed, since broadcast and multicast packets are intended for multiple destinations, we cannot have receivers sending back acknowledgments. Because all these acknowledgments, if sent at the same time, will collide with each other. So no use. If you had to desynchronize the acknowledgments transmissions, that would be very very complicated. And it would increase the overhead of the protocol. So that's done. So the choice that they made was, well, if a packet is broadcast or multicast, the transmitter of course needs to sense the channel. If the channel is idle, transmit. If the channel is busy, of course you have to perform the kickoff procedure because you have to wait. But then once you access the channel and transmit, that's it. Okay, you are done. Because you don't care if the packet was received successfully or unsuccessfully. You are done. Okay, so broadcast and multicast packets are transmitted only once. So you may need to run the kickoff procedure for those data packets. But just if when you want to access the channel, you sense the channel as busy the first time.
